clue.text: City worth touring when idle

indicators.note: touring means going round and about, so the letters of the two words travel into a new order

explanation.surface: A recommendation to visit a city when you have time on your hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges the eight letters of WHEN IDLE; 'worth' only joins the surface, a city worth touring.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital district of India is a city, the seat of its national government.

clue.text: Vessel sending up comedy series? Not half

indicators.note: sending up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
not half says one of the two equal halves of the title is dropped

parts.note: 'Allo 'Allo! was a long-running BBC sitcom set in wartime France

explanation.surface: A pot that mocks a TV comedy, though only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' leaves ALLO from the doubled title, and 'sending up' turns it to read OLLA. 'Allo 'Allo! is a British TV sitcom set in occupied France.
explanation.definitionFit: An olla is an earthenware cooking pot or jar, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Eat food and bring up the last traces

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up the last letter lifts it from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to eat food is to ingest it

explanation.surface: A diner eats and then is sick, leaving only remnants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring up the last' moves the final T of INGEST to the front; 'bring up' pretends to mean vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinges are slight traces or hints, as of colour or a feeling.

clue.text: Region for Asian prince to hold gymkhana — tele-vised? Contrariwise

indicators.note: to hold suggests the prince holding the gymkhana, but read the other way the words hold the letters
contrariwise says swap the holder and the held: the clue words contain the answer rather than the prince containing them

explanation.surface: A ruler's land is offered to host a televised horse show, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests KHAN holding a word; 'Contrariwise' flips that, so 'gymkhana — tele' holds the answer, which sits across the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A khanate is the territory ruled by a khan, a title for Central Asian rulers.

clue.text: He tells the story about corruption on Scottish island

indicators.note: about means turning round, so the whole stack of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts a tale of corruption on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece sits 'on' the other, and 'about' turns the whole column round, giving ROTARRAN read upwards. Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the voice that relates the events of a story.

clue.text: Places whereat to water around the stormy south and places wherein to dry

indicators.note: around says the watering places surround the other letters

parts.note: oases are spots in a desert where travellers find water

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters of the word are tossed about

explanation.surface: A contrast between desert watering holes and buildings for drying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' makes THOUS, which the watering places go 'around'; 'the' is a link. Oast houses are kilns for drying hops, common in Kent; the clue plays on two kinds of place.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast house is a kiln building in which hops are dried for brewing.

clue.text: Lacking name, Gates's baby loss adjusters?

indicators.note: lacking says one letter is missing from the software name

parts.note: Bill Gates's Microsoft created the Windows operating system

explanation.surface: An insurance query about a tech mogul's product missing its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' drops the N for name from WINDOWS. 'loss adjusters' are insurance assessors, but here they are people adjusting to bereavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Widows are women who must adjust to the loss of a husband, a whimsical reading of an insurance job title.

clue.text: Round outskirts of Luton my fellow passengers and I land? Nearly, nearly

parts.note: a speaker with fellow passengers says we

indicators.note: round says the trimmed word goes around the edge letters of the town
nearly means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to light is to come down and settle, as a bird lands

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An air passenger near Luton airport wonders if the plane has almost landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts the verb to LIGH, and 'Round' wraps it around Luton's outer letters, making LLNIGH. 'Nearly' is used twice: the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-nigh is an old-fashioned adverb for almost or nearly.

clue.text: Slowly a serviceman slips into a party

indicators.note: slips into means one group of letters is quietly inserted into another

parts.note: a do is a party
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier sneaks into a party, moving slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'a' belongs to the piece after it; the serviceman pair slips into the party pair after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction meaning to be played slowly.

clue.text: It's dismal, reporting Roman theatres

indicators.note: reporting signals words as they would be heard spoken

parts.note: 'oh dear!' is what one says on finding things dismal

explanation.surface: A gloomy report about ancient theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reporting' means said aloud: the exclamation of dismay sounds like ODEA. The answer is a Latin plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Odea is the plural of odeum, a roofed theatre for music in ancient Rome or Greece.

clue.text: In years, about 30 — an integer oddly divisible by zero

indicators.note: oddly means in an odd, irregular way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: zero is the figure 0, read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A mathematical puzzle about dividing an integer by zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges AN INTEGER plus O for zero; 'divisible by' only joins the maths surface, and 30 is years, not a number to divide.
explanation.definitionFit: A human generation is reckoned at roughly thirty years, the span between parents and children.

clue.text: Seeks to deceive more than one bank

definitions.meaning: a poker player ... to pretend a strong hand
steep cliffs or banks, often beside a river

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pretending and a plural noun for steep riverbanks.

clue.text: Get one a profit from knocking down this antique instrument

indicators.note: knocking down means demolishing, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Selling off an antique piano at auction might make you a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking down' is auction-speak for selling, but here it rearranges ONE plus A PROFIT; 'Get' and 'from' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortepiano is the early piano of Mozart's day, now an antique instrument.

clue.text: England cricketer bags duck (English getting the bird)

indicators.note: bags means takes in, so the cricketer holds the round letter

parts.note: Fred Titmus was an England spin bowler
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricketer is out for nought, and the English get a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: TITMUS 'bags' the O to make TITMOUS, then E for English is added. Fred Titmus played cricket for England; a duck is a score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is the fuller name for the tit, a small songbird.

clue.text: Middle part of statement's omitted from free balance

indicators.note: omitted from says a letter is left out of the word that follows

parts.note: to free is to liberate

indicators.note: the middle part of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

explanation.surface: Part of a statement is cut from a document about free balance.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'statement' is E; dropping one E from LIBERATE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To librate is to sway or oscillate like a balance before coming to rest.

clue.text: Ma scared with ferret running around commercial woodland

indicators.note: running around suggests letters dashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened mother with a ferret loose around a plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scared with' only sets the scene of a frightened mother; the anagram signal is 'running around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree farm is a plantation where trees are grown as a commercial crop.

clue.text: They remove evidence of one-age exchange for 'is and 'ers

indicators.note: an exchange for says one piece is swapped out and another put in

parts.note: the words with their H dropped, as in Cockney speech, run together
I is the Roman numeral for one
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A Cockney remark about towels marked 'his' and 'hers'.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the I in ISERS for ERA gives the answer; the dropped H mimics Cockney speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasers rub out marks, removing the evidence of mistakes.

clue.text: Rabelais novel may be exalted

indicators.note: novel means new, so the author's name is made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A French writer's novel might be held in high esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges RABELAIS, the French Renaissance author.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raisable can be lifted up, which is what exalted literally means.

clue.text: Mounted on a horse, I had savings — take some

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the letters go upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: I had shortens to I'd
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: A rider on horseback dips into savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' turns I'D upwards to DI in this down clue; 'on' puts it above the horse. Dipping into savings is taking some of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip into savings is to draw on some of the money put aside.

clue.text: Summer in Paris in clubs, right new tie being worn with the others

indicators.note: in says the clubs letter sits inside the French word

parts.note: ete is French for summer
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: new says these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A summer outfit in Paris: clubs and a new tie worn with everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes 'in' ETE, giving ETCE; 'new' rearranges R plus TIE into TERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Et ceteri is Latin for 'and the other people', the masculine plural of et cetera.

clue.text: Unexceptionally, one invading erstwhile old-time empire

indicators.note: invading says the single letter forces its way into the other word
erstwhile means former or ex-, so that stretch is removed

parts.note: the Ottoman Empire ruled Turkey and beyond for centuries
OT stands for Old Testament, the old-time scripture
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tale of an invasion of the old Ottoman empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erstwhile' means ex-, so OT (Old Testament, old-time) leaves the empire, making TOMAN; 'one' invades it.
explanation.definitionFit: To a man means every single person without exception.

clue.text: Captain's obsession to take back state

indicators.note: back says the taken letters are read in reverse
to take signals that the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is obsessed with recapturing a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'take back' wholly to the reversal, leaving the hidden word unsignalled; 'to take' lifts AINSOB from across 'Captain's obsession' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosnia is a European country, part of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

clue.text: Less diminutive horse in nursery found in the final frame

indicators.note: found in says the horse letters sit inside the frame

parts.note: a bier is the frame on which a coffin is carried at a funeral
gee-gee is baby talk for a horse, abbreviated GG

explanation.surface: A rocking horse is found inside the final frame of a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the final frame' sounds like the end of a film, but it is the frame that carries a coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigger means larger, the opposite of more diminutive.

clue.text: Saw fist broken gatecrashing meeting

indicators.note: gatecrashing means barging into, so the broken letters enter another word

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

indicators.note: broken says the letters are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A violent gatecrasher breaks his fist at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes TISF; 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun for a proverb, and 'meeting' means fulfilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfying a requirement is meeting it.

clue.text: Endure an ill-mannered fellow

definitions.meaning: a ... can be a gruff, uncouth person

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means put up with and the noun describes a surly, boorish man.

clue.text: Documents on female sponger

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a bum is a scrounger

explanation.surface: Paperwork kept on a woman living off others.
explanation.walkthrough: BUM goes on top of F.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork or documents.

clue.text: In the money, he's one wanting to deposit yen

definitions.note: the definition describes one who is in the money

indicators.note: to deposit means to put down, so the letter is set aside and dropped

parts.note: someone wanting something is a yearner
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A rich man wants to pay in some Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping Y (yen) from YEARNER leaves one who earns; 'deposit' looks like banking but means put down.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is a person bringing in income, someone in the money.

clue.text: Jollies restricted too warm clothes

parts.note: Jollies is the nickname for the Royal Marines, the RM

indicators.note: restricted means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: also means too

explanation.surface: Marines are kept in overly warm clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' trims ALSO to ALS. Jollies is navy slang for the Royal Marines, giving THE RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermals are warm underclothes worn for insulation in cold weather.
